title: Glass Mastery
kicker: READING THE REBOUND · EXIT CHOICE · BAJADA · CONTRA-PARED · LOW BALLS · MOVING UP
opener_line: The glass gives you time. These drills teach you what to buy with it.
intro_title: Turning the wall into a choice.
intro: At level three you can get the ball back off the glass. The next step is getting something useful from it. A rebound hands you a moment of time, and time lets you choose. These ten drills put a decision into every wall ball: where it will drop, how high it will come out, where the opponents are standing, and whether your pair can move forward afterwards. Each one begins with a feed and ends with a choice.

Work through them roughly in order. The first drills sharpen the read of the rebound itself. The middle ones add a target that changes with the opponent. The last ones join the exit to whatever happens next, so the glass becomes the opening of a pattern rather than a rescue. Keep the feeder honest, too. A feed that is too kind trains a read you will never need in a match.

pillars.title: Read before moving
pillars.text: Pace, height and spin of the feed tell you where the rebound will drop. Decide early, then go.

pillars.title: Wait for height
pillars.text: Let the ball come to you after the wall. The contact height decides which shots are still possible.

pillars.title: Look up once
pillars.text: A single glance at the opponents before contact turns a safe exit into a chosen one.

pillars.title: Exit, then act
pillars.text: A good exit is only half a pattern. Know whether your pair now holds the back or moves up.

box.label: THE REBOUND RULE
box.text: High off the glass, you may attack. Low, you lift it or slow it down. Past you, use your own wall. The ball picks the shot; your job is to read it first.

drills.title: Call the drop.
drills.summary: F feeds into the back glass and A must call where the ball will drop to hip height before moving to play it.
drills.setup: A starts on the service line, drive side. F stands 2–3 m from the net on the far side with a basket. Three cones sit one, two and three metres off the back glass.
run: F mixes pace and height. A turns side-on the moment the ball crosses the net.
Before the ball touches the glass, A calls 'one', 'two' or 'three' for the cone where it will drop to hip height after the rebound.
A moves to that cone, lets the ball come down to the hip and plays a controlled cross-court ball into T1.
F confirms each call. Twelve balls, then switch to the revés side, where B hits and A calls for B.
drills.decision: Where will this ball be playable? Pace, depth and bounce height tell you how far it will come back off the glass. Commit to a spot early instead of drifting with the ball.
drills.watch: Calling late, after the rebound, which turns reading into reacting. The call must come before the glass; F counts a missing call as wrong.
drills.up: F adds side spin and the odd double-wall feed into the corner, so the rebound angle changes as well as the distance.
drills.down: Use two cones only, near and far, and let F feed at one steady pace for the first six balls.
drills.pass: Nine correct calls and nine clean returns out of twelve on each side.
drills.caption: A calls the cone before the ball reaches the glass, moves to it and plays cross-court into T1.

drills.title: Lob on the clock.
drills.summary: Off a back-glass feed, A lobs deep cross-court while C and D rush the net, beating a two-beat count.
drills.setup: A at the back, drive side. F feeds from beside the far net post. C and D start on their service line. Mark a zone in the last 3 m, cross-court from A.
run: F feeds firmly into A's back glass. As the feed leaves F's racket, C and D sprint forward to their volley positions.
F calls 'one' as the ball strikes the glass and 'two' a beat later. A must lob before 'two', even off an imperfect contact.
The lob travels cross-court over C, high enough to clear a raised racket and long enough for the zone.
If C or D reach it, they play a bandeja and the point runs live for three shots. Ten feeds, then rotate.
drills.decision: Lob now or wait for a sweeter contact? Against a closing pair, the half-second you take is the half-second they use to reach the net. Early and high beats late and perfect.
drills.watch: Low, flat lobs struck in a hurry. Stay under the ball and finish the racket high, so the lob peaks above the opponents, not at their rackets.
drills.up: F shortens the count to a single call at the glass, or C and D start a metre further forward.
drills.down: Drop the count and let C and D close at walking pace while A finds the height.
drills.pass: Seven lobs out of ten land in the zone without being intercepted.
drills.caption: C and D close as F feeds. A must lob from the glass into T1 before the second beat.

drills.title: Glass to the feet.
drills.summary: After a back-glass rebound, A plays a slow chiquita at the feet of C, who walks in from the service line.
drills.setup: A at the back, drive side. F feeds from the far centre. C starts on the far service line, cross-court from A. Mark a zone between that service line and the net.
run: F feeds at medium pace into the back glass. As F's racket meets the ball, C starts walking forward.
A lets the rebound drop below the hip, then plays a soft, slightly sliced ball that crosses low and falls into the zone.
C must volley it. If C volleys up from below the tape, A scores; if C volleys down, C scores.
After eight balls, C varies the approach, sometimes rushing right up to the net. A lobs when C is already close.
drills.decision: How close is the volleyer? Near the service line, a ball at the feet forces a lift. Tight to the net, a chiquita sits up for them; lob instead.
drills.watch: Hitting the chiquita too hard, so it skids past C's feet into an easy half-volley. Slow the racket, open the face and land it short.
drills.up: Add D at the net, so A must also keep the ball away from a second volleyer.
drills.down: C stays still on the service line and F feeds slower, so the ball sits up off the glass.
drills.pass: A wins at least five of the eight points in each block.
drills.caption: C walks in as the feed is struck. A drops the glass ball into T1 so C has to volley up.

drills.title: Three-door corner.
drills.summary: F feeds into A's corner, then moves; A reads F's new position and picks lob, chiquita or drive.
drills.setup: A on the drive side, about 2 m from the back glass. F starts on the far service line holding a few balls. Mark zones T1 deep cross-court, T2 short cross-court, T3 deep middle.
run: F feeds firmly so the ball strikes A's side glass, then the back glass, and runs out towards the middle.
As the ball reaches the second wall, F moves forward to the net, holds the service line or drops back, in no fixed order.
A chooses: lob over a net player, chiquita at the feet of a service-line player, firm drive to the deep middle against a back player.
Twelve feeds into the drive corner, then twelve into the revés corner with B hitting.
drills.decision: Where is the opponent, and what can they do with each answer? Look up after the second wall, not before; the last picture before contact chooses the shot.
drills.watch: Never looking at F. Take one quick glance as the ball leaves the second wall, then eyes back on the ball for contact.
drills.up: F delays the move until the ball is almost at A's racket, or adds a fake step before settling.
drills.down: F moves early, while the feed is still in the air, and uses only two positions: net or back.
drills.pass: Nine right choices out of twelve, seven of them in the matching zone.
drills.caption: Side glass, back glass, then a glance: F's new position decides lob (T1), chiquita (T2) or drive (T3).

drills.title: High rebound, hard choice.
drills.summary: F lobs over A at different heights; A attacks the rebound with a bajada only when it comes out high enough.
drills.setup: A starts at net position, drive side. F lobs from the far back court. C stands at the far net position, cross-court, as an opponent who has lobbed and closed.
run: F varies the lobs: some high and deep, others lower and flatter, so they come off the glass at the waist or below.
A turns, runs back beside the side glass and lets the ball rebound off the back glass, staying side-on with the racket up.
Well above the waist, ideally at the shoulder: A plays a bajada down, deep cross-court or at C's feet. Lower: A lobs over C.
C plays the ball and the point runs live for two more shots. Three sets of ten, then B works the revés side.
drills.decision: How high is the ball as it leaves the glass? From the shoulder you can hit down with control. Lower, a hard ball tends to rise into C's volley; a lob keeps you in the point.
drills.watch: Attacking every rebound because it feels like the drill. A calls 'hit' or 'lob' aloud as the ball strikes the glass, then sticks to it.
drills.up: C may step in to cut off weak bajadas, and F adds lower, faster lobs that look attackable but are not.
drills.down: F lobs slower, and A catches the first rebound of each set to judge the height.
drills.pass: Eight correct hit-or-lob calls out of ten, and no bajada struck from below the waist.
drills.caption: A retreats under the lob and reads the rebound: attack deep cross-court if it comes out high, lob over C if not.

drills.title: Off your own wall.
drills.summary: F feeds balls that beat A into the corner; A hits them into A's own back glass so they rebound over the net.
drills.setup: A on the drive side, about 2 m from the back glass. F feeds from the far service line, aiming deep at A's corner.
run: F feeds fast and low so the ball gets past A after the bounce, too quickly to turn and play normally.
A turns the back to the net, gets the racket behind the ball and hits upwards into the back glass, roughly two metres up.
The ball rebounds over A's head and drops over the net. Height matters more than pace; a low rebound dies in the net.
Half the feeds are reachable; A plays those normally. Twelve feeds, then switch to the revés corner.
drills.decision: Is this a real emergency? Use the contra-pared only when the ball has gone past you and no ordinary exit is left. If it will still come off the glass, wait.
drills.watch: Hitting the mesh or the very corner. A ball that touches your own mesh loses the point (FIP Rule 13), so pick a spot high on the back glass.
drills.up: F feeds off the side glass first, and C waits at the net to volley weak escapes.
drills.down: F feeds slower, by hand, so A can set up the upward swing calmly.
drills.pass: Eight of twelve contra-pareds land in, with no wrong choice on the reachable feeds.
drills.caption: The feed beats A into the corner. A hits up into the back glass and the rebound carries over the net.

drills.title: Low ball down the middle.
drills.summary: Off the back glass, A drives low and firm through the gap between C and D, where neither clearly owns the volley.
drills.setup: A and B start deep. C and D wait at the far net position, rackets up. F feeds from behind them. Mark a narrow channel down the middle of their half.
run: F feeds deep so the ball comes off A's back glass at the waist or below. A moves forward with it.
A plays a flat or lightly sliced drive just over the net through the channel, below their rackets, towards their hips.
A winner, or a volley played up from below the tape, scores for A; a volley hit down scores for C and D.
Eight balls to A, eight to B. Then C and D cheat sideways; A and B must find the bigger gap.
drills.decision: Is the middle open? When C and D stand wide, the seam is the safest low ball: the net is lowest there and both may hesitate. When they squeeze together, go wide.
drills.watch: Lifting the drive to shoulder height, where either volleyer can punch it. Contact in front of the body, swing level, finish low.
drills.up: C and D may close the middle as soon as the ball leaves the glass, so the read comes later.
drills.down: Remove D and leave a single volleyer standing to one side of the channel.
drills.pass: Ten of sixteen drives either win the point or force an upward volley.
drills.caption: A takes the rebound early and drives low through T1, the seam between the two volleyers.

drills.title: The ball that dies.
drills.summary: F feeds heavy slice so the ball skids into the back glass and leaves it low; A must get under it and still place it.
drills.setup: A on the drive side at the back. F feeds with slice from the far service line. Mark a deep cross-court zone and a short zone just past the net.
run: F's sliced feeds land close to the glass, hit it with little height and drop quickly, often below the knee.
A bends early, with the knees rather than the back, and gets the racket face under the ball before it falls further.
Knee height or above: A lifts a deep cross-court lob into T1. Lower: A plays a soft, safe ball into T2.
F mixes sliced and plain feeds without warning. Ten balls per set; A reports how many sat below the knee.
drills.decision: How much room is there between ball and floor? The lower it sits, the fewer options remain. Pick the shot still possible, not the one you planned.
drills.watch: Waiting at the usual spot for a rebound that never arrives. Sliced balls come off shorter and lower; move closer to the wall and stay down.
drills.up: F adds sliced feeds into the corner, so the ball loses height across two walls.
drills.down: F uses less slice and feeds from closer, so the drop after the glass is gentler.
drills.pass: Seven of ten balls back over the net, at least four of them in T1.
drills.caption: The sliced feed stays low off the glass. A closes in, gets under it and lifts deep into T1.

drills.title: Every ball off a wall.
drills.summary: Two pairs rally cooperatively from the back, every ball reaching the back glass before it is played; after ten, the point goes live.
drills.setup: Both pairs start about 2 m from their back glass. One ball, no feeder. Any player starts with an underarm ball deep into the far court.
run: Rally cooperatively. Every ball must bounce and touch the back glass before it is played, so every shot must reach the wall.
Count aloud together. A ball played before it reaches the glass, or one that dies short of it, sends the count back to zero.
When the count reaches ten, either pair may attack or move forward. From that moment the point is played under normal rules.
The pair that wins the live point scores one. A rally that never reaches ten scores nothing. Play to seven, then change partners.
drills.decision: When the rally goes live, who strikes first? Use the cooperative phase to find which opponent handles the glass worst, then aim the first live ball there.
drills.watch: Pushing the ball deep with too much pace, so the rebound carries into the middle and the rally becomes a scramble. Use height, not speed, to get your depth.
drills.up: After ten, the pair that struck the tenth ball must lob, and the other pair may take the net at once.
drills.down: Count to six, and side-glass balls count as well as back-glass balls.
drills.pass: Both pairs reach ten in five rallies in a row before scoring starts.
drills.caption: Every shot must reach the back glass before it is played. At ten the point goes live.

drills.title: Exit and climb.
drills.summary: When A's lob off the glass truly beats the net pair, A and B take the net together; otherwise they hold the back.
drills.setup: A and B at the back. C and D at net position on the far side. C starts each point by feeding firmly into the back glass on A's side.
run: C feeds into A's back glass. A plays the exit: a lob over C or D, or a low ball if the lob is not on.
When A sees the lob will pass the net pair and turn them, A calls 'up' and both advance side by side.
If the lob is short, or C and D can play an overhead, A calls 'stay', and the pair holds the back of the court and defends.
Play the point out. A point won at the net after an 'up' call scores two. Swap the feeding role and sides after ten points.
drills.decision: Has the lob bought enough time? You climb only when the opponents are turning their backs to chase. A lob they can smash is not a ticket to the net.
drills.watch: Only the hitter going forward while the partner stays back. B moves on A's call, and the two arrive level, like one unit.
drills.up: C and D answer good lobs with a counter-lob, so A and B must arrive balanced.
drills.down: Remove D, so A and B face a single net player and the read is simpler.
drills.pass: A correct 'up' or 'stay' call on eight of ten points, judged by the waiting pair.
drills.caption: A's lob sends C back to chase. On A's 'up' call, A and B climb to the net together.
